newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss-based private air firm changes name.
newsitem.headline: Swiss-based private air firm changes name.

text.p: Swiss-based private air company PetrolAir, which has transported many heads of state and bills itself as the most discrete and exclusive in the world, said on Thursday it had changed its name to PrivatAir.

The company, which operates out of Geneva's Cointrin airport, currently has a fleet of three luxuriously-equipped jets -- a Gulfstream IV for 10 passengers, a Boeing 737 carrying 27 and a Boeing 757 for 44 passengers.
But in a statement on the name change, it said it was waiting to take delivery shortly of a six-seater Hawker 800 "which will answer the more limited needs of some clients."

Founded in 1981 as an internal airline for the Swiss-based Petrola group of companies, it was granted a licence by the country's federal aviation authorities in 1995 to operate as a private commercial carrier.
The company has a staff of 40 people, including 16 pilots. It says its aircraft are maintained "to the highest security standards" mainly by engineers from British airline BA and Germany's Lufthansa.
